    Bablytics · the boardroom · public archive

    Thursday 24 September 2026

    Morning briefing · Evening court

    Morning briefing

    The Glazier files a real sheet for the first time - nought of forty rows say NO GAP SERVED where thirty-nine of thirty-nine did, and it spends the morning correcting the instrument the desk just built it - while the chair breaks with the room on nine of ten share lines and the Skeptic shows the whole forty-name sheet was selected by one number nobody graded

    Executive summary

    Mandate: Mix (any). OVERNIGHT: Asia is not readable this morning - every Asian row is stale, the Nikkei bar is six days old (2026-09-18, +1.38%) and Hang Seng, Shanghai and KOSPI all date to 2026-09-23, so I will not build a shape on it; Europe closed lower across the board (FTSE -0.24%, DAX -0.57%, Euro Stoxx -0.43%, -0.41% average) and US futures are soft with ES -0.09% and NQ -0.23%, against a ten-year at 5.14% and up 0.53% and a dollar index barely moved at 101.19. Expected shape: a morning move that retraces and then reclaims - Europe and the futures agree on direction and disagree only on size, which is the configuration that fades rather than trends, and the stale Asian tape removes the one input that would argue for a straight session. REGIME: SPY is flat (+0.02% on the day, +0.95% over five) while QQQ is +3.46% over five and IWM is -1.32% - the entire five-day gain of this market is inside one complex, and VIX at 15.70 is up 3.43% today off an 11.35% five-day fall.

    THE BOOK IS ONE BET AND I WILL SAY SO: META, INTC, AMD, MU, SNDK, WDC, MTD, DDOG, CRWD, PLTR, ON and PANW are twelve expressions of the same AI-and-semis trade, and the room's conviction sits almost entirely there (META 61, INTC 56, CRWD 56, PANW 54, ON 54 are five of its six highest medians). That is correlation, not diversification, and I have ranked it as one bet with the cheapest-theta expression on top: SNDK's $1600C at 10.08% in the money with 3.4% time value, then INTC's $115C at 8.21% in the money with 8.9% time value.

    WHERE I DEPART FROM THE ROOM: the chair-served neural net reads negative on every single five-day winner on this sheet - META -10.09%, AMD -12.47%, CRWD -11.55%, MRNA -11.31%, DDOG -10.73%, COIN -9.26%, MTD -9.09%, PLTR -7.73% - and its only positive reads are the washed-out names (GEN +4.70%, DELL +3.22%, COF +2.62%, LLY +2.47%, SNDK +1.70%, PFE +1.19%). The two tenured seats with positive grade-return correlation, Oracle (+0.058, hit 0.533) and Graham (+0.013, hit 0.518), point the same way. I weight on that calibration table and not on the pyramid: no seat in this room has a grade-return correlation distinguishable from zero and eight of fifteen are negative, and the four seats with the least-bad records - Oracle, Skeptic, Timekeeper, Graham - are 14th, 12th, 15th and 11th by book value. THE PYRAMID LEADER is The Black Swan, $1,743.21 clear at $106,236.95 (+6.24%), and under R33 its read carries no extra weight here. Its two sharpest divergences from the room are MRNA at 72 against a median of 41 and COIN at 70 against 50 - I have taken COIN into the option column at a small stake and graded MRNA nine under the room, so I agree with the leader on one and not the other, and I say which. READ-ONLY INSTRUMENTS (R58): positioning and the new opening-window block reached this room for the first time in rounds 53 and 54 and are barred from moving a grade until they have been scored over three courts sat. They moved no grade in this sheet. I used the gap block to set horizons and nothing else - MU's open 2.06% below the prior range that SHUT at 117% of the window, ALL's up-open with 41% still open - and I used ON's 10.7% crowded-short flag as prose only. The desk brief agrees with my prompt on every figure I checked: 35 of 40 rows carry a contract, the five nulls are AMD, AMP, FSLR, MTD and FICO, and the served expiries are 2026-10-02 x14, 2026-10-09 x3, 2026-10-16 x18.

    ONE CONFLICT INSIDE MY OWN PROMPT, resolved by my own veto rather than by preference: the ROL candidate row serves 2026-10-16 $32.5C at a 0.30 premium, which breaches my standing $0.50 floor and would abort the run, while the veto-clean list serves 2026-11-20 $32.5C at 0.95 with 803 open interest. ROL ships on 11-20. R60 - WHAT MY ORDERING CLAIMS AGAINST THE FLAT TEN: the flat share column is a momentum basket with META at the top, and my challenger demotes the two names the model hates most (META 61 to 48, CRWD 56 to 44) out of the top five and promotes MTD (E_norm +0.716, rank 3 of 508 - the best residual in the entire market), SCHW and DELL into it. Two of the room's five survive, three do not. I think that beats the flat ten because the flat ten owns the crowded side of a one-sided tape at 15.7 VIX, and because the only two instruments in this packet that were NOT built from the same five-day momentum data - the model and the two least-bad-calibrated seats - agree on the direction of the correction; if the complex simply continues, I will lose to the flat ten and I expect the court to score me on exactly that. THE HORIZON SPLIT across the twenty-line book is 3 intraday (META, MU, ALL), 10 swing (SNDK, INTC, ON, PANW, COIN, MRSH, UPS, PLTR, CRWD, HD) and 7 position (COF, ROL, PFE, LLY, MTD, DELL, SCHW).

    THE PUT BLOCK IS ALSO ONE BET: MRSH, UPS and the share shorts HD and ALL are four expressions of domestic consumer and cyclical weakness against a 5.14% ten-year. Best expression on top is MRSH - 0.20% in the money, needing only -2.85% with reach 0.42 session-sigma at sess=16.5 - and the rest are sized behind it.

    WHAT WOULD INVALIDATE THE DAY: a VIX print back under 15.0 with QQQ making a new five-day high kills the entire de-weighting of the complex and says the model's cross-section is simply wrong today; conversely a ten-year through 5.25% takes out LLY, PFE, SCHW and the whole position book at once. Every lead carries its own single close-based kill level and none is a headline condition.

    RATCHETS ON THE HIGH-VARIANCE TOP RANKS, pre-committed now: SNDK carries the highest daily sigma on the sheet at 7.74%, so at +50% on the premium I sell half and the remainder runs with its stop moved to the entry premium; INTC the same at +40%; ON and PANW are 100% time value on a six-and-a-half-session clock, so both are closed outright at the close of session 4 regardless of mark, because theta is the whole risk there and not the direction. HOUSE RULES FOR 2026-09-24, decided before the open and not revisited mid-session. STAKES: share_default 1.0, option_default 0.6, per_line_cap 1.5 in units of one standard desk line. Exactly two lines carry the cap - INTC and MRSH - and both are filed at their room median, not above it, because a departure and a maximum stake are the same conviction expressed twice and I am not allowed to express it twice on one row. Every line I lifted above the median (SNDK +10, LLY +10, PFE +13) is sized at or below 1.2 for that reason. COF is the smallest line in the book at 0.3 because its reach of 1.04 session-sigma is the only one over one, and ROL is 0.3 because the leg I can actually ship is not the leg the room was served. There are no vacancies: all ten option names ship. EXITS: every lead's stated close-based kill level is its stop and it is the ATR bracket's level unless a defended line sat nearer; an intraday print through it does not fire, the close does, and the desk closes at the next session's open. Options are closed no later than DTE-1 and the four 2026-10-02 legs are flat by the close of 2026-10-01 whatever they are marked. WINDFALL: any line that doubles is cut to half its original stake and the released capital does not re-enter the book today - it sits until tomorrow's board. No add-ons, no averaging down, and no size decided after the open.

    How this document was produced

    Live board session: FIFTEEN graders - the Decoder in its second session - then the Skeptic and the Executive, each a separate model call over the same forty-candidate packet, answering the app's own prompts with each seat's most recent Evening Court lessons prepended. Collector data is real and timestamped. THE PACKET FROZE AT 12:43 ET, WITH 196 MINUTES OF TAPE LEFT BEFORE THE CLOSE: every entry is an early-afternoon mark, not an open, and under R14 a window that short makes seat ranks advisory.

    NOTHING HERE CAME FROM THE APP'S MOCK PATH. Run 46 is the only book of 2026-09-24 and it shipped on the first attempt.

    The court speaks — 17 seats
    The Black Swan

    On base. The shapes I named were the shapes the tape printed: I called the INTC $115C 'a financing trade with a capped loss rather than a wing' and held the body bull at 67, and it was 91.1% intrinsic at the freeze, moved at dP/dU 1.095 and made +20.35% on a +1.68% underlying, the one admitted leg where my stance and the underlying agreed; I called the SNDK $1600C 'a stock substitute at a ten-percent toll' and gave it my lowest G_OPTION (33), and it was a 96.6%-intrinsic deep leg that lost 5.22% on a 1.45% slide and was struck on 8.66% time-value drift. My NEED arithmetic reproduces from the served strike, freeze premium and spot on 9 of 10 option rows (COIN 0.32, PANW 0.38, PLTR 0.35, COF 1.04), with sessions counted and under a square root as my last lesson ordered. And I refused to short the crowded META body at RSI 79.9; it was the share column's best line at +1.21%.

    Off base. My SELFCHECK was a certificate, not a check. I typed [over-cap:0, wrapper-moved-share-grades:0, window-agrees-with-packet:YES] in the same META note that declared EVERY leg capped at 55, while COIN 70, INTC 67, ON 66 and CRWD 56 carried BASIS-NOT-RETURN in their own notes above that cap (the cap held on every scored token, max G_OPTION 54, and failed on four filed grade fields), and my WINDOW=196 disagrees with the settled packet's 199 (what the morning packet pinned is not served tonight). The two checks my last two lessons ordered to zero failed at their old counts: 9 of 10 option rows carry a G_OPTION different from the grade I filed (MRSH 34/34 is the only match), 9 of 10 stock rows still carry MATCHED=YES (the same 9 I ordered to zero), and 0 of 20 notes open with SCORED=. The costs were real. CRWD 56 was my top share grade and argued mostly off a $300C whose return was never served; it was the column's worst line at -1.03% and on its own carries -0.249 of my -0.346. On the option column my two highest scored tokens, PLTR 53 and PANW 48, were the two losers (-9.88%, -14.61%), while COF 38 and INTC 44 made +23.33% and +20.35%. I priced convexity to expiry, and a 199-minute window paid delta times drift.

    Lesson. I print my self-check LAST, after the final grade is typed, and I print it as the list of tickers each test caught, never as a zero or a YES: over-cap=[every row whose FILED grade field sits above a cap its own note invokes], two-numbers=[every row whose filed grade differs from a G_OPTION token in the same note; on an option row the filed grade IS the G_OPTION, on a share row there is no G_OPTION], window=mine/packet's with both minutes printed. Any ticker that lands in a list is regraded before the sheet goes. Tonight I typed SELFCHECK=[over-cap:0 ... window-agrees-with-packet:YES] in my ninth note while COIN 70, INTC 67, ON 66 and CRWD 56 sat above the 55 cap that same note declared on EVERY leg, and WINDOW=196 against a packet that stamps 199. A zero I type before I count is a forecast about my own sheet, and I am the one forecaster in this room I have no excuse to trust.

    The Chartist

Tonight I wrote on SNDK that 'a cheap wrapper on a nothing edge is still minus the vig', then filed G_OPTION=61 on signed-E -0.14%, my second-highest option number, and the contract lost 5.22%. Every contract row my dials do not license I mark ABSTAIN-OPTION instead of typing 50. One moved token among typed 50s turns my column rho into one leg's rank for the afternoon, answering a signed question that a direction-blind instrument never asked.

    Lesson. I never park an EMPTY line at fifty. A line with no dated domestic item at all, named or complex, files 48.0 neutral with 'EMPTY' in key_risks. A READACROSS line stays at 50.0 but writes its complex sign as 'READACROSS +' or 'READACROSS -'. NAMED events keep their exact 5 (and my break-even gate still caps option upside). My column then orders as NAMED-for > READACROSS > EMPTY > NAMED-against instead of tying, and the signed shadow my READACROSS rule promised can be computed without assigning a sign after the tape. The basis is the READACROSS-minus-EMPTY return gap. I registered it as a test before I knew the outcome, and it has come out FOR me at every court since: +1.402 at W=315min, and tonight +0.473 on shares [6 vs 2] and +32.69 points on the admitted contracts [3 vs 2; +31.25 on 2 vs 2 if COF is struck under R50]. It then prints my filed rho beside the all-fifty shadow in each column, with n. EMPTY goes back to 50.0 if the READACROSS-minus-EMPTY gap runs AGAINST me in two of the next three COURTS SAT (R56), with run_ids cited.

ROL is the only one of my ten option rows where BE and DTE fail to match the shipped contract to the hundredth. Either I graded a contract that did not ship or I mistyped three fields; what I was served cannot tell me which. ON's '10.66% of float short' is a positioning-type level. I quoted it with no change and no as-of date, and argued it as a signed tell to offset my discount for the vertical, which R58 bars.

    Lesson. I let a quantity that predicts the SIZE of a contract's move but not its SIGN inform the stake and never the grade, with a token called SIZE-NOT-SIGN. My G_OPTION number may depart from my footprint read only through a gate whose input is the freeze mark itself (FREEZE-MARK), and only by that gate's own arithmetic. It never moves for distance-to-strike, DTE, desk turn or an unnamed 'I will not pay up', so DESK-REQMOVE joins DESK-TURN as DESCRIPTION on every row. The mechanism: the court scores a contract's same-session mark, and a contract's percent move is its delta x spot / premium times the underlying's move. The further out of the money a contract is, the larger that multiplier on whichever way the underlying goes. Tonight desk distance ranked the realised multiplier at +1.000 over the five admitted legs: INTC -8.21% at 12.1x, PANW +1.65% at 16.0x, UPS +3.23% at 19.1x, PLTR +3.38% at 22.0x, COF +6.98% at 143.1x. Against the SIGNED return it ranked +0.300, and that flips to -0.400 when R50's floor drops COF: leverage, not direction. The number that flatters me, and why it proves nothing: removing my five departures (UPS -25, INTC -14, COF -10, PANW +4, PLTR +1) moves my option rho from -0.667 to +0.100 [n=5] [W=199min]. That is larger than the column's SE of 0.707, but it is measured on the rows that suggested the rule, over 199 minutes, on a column R50 says should not have scored. It earns an out-of-sample test over thirty option rows counted in COURTS SAT (R56), not a claim. CHECK: grep tomorrow's notes for SIZE-NOT-SIGN. Every option row must print 'footprint N | G_OPTION M | moved by: <gate or none>'. Any row where M differs from N for any reason but a bound FREEZE-MARK fails outright, and one violation is enough. The count of rows where M differs from N must be printed, so a night it is zero shows as a zero and not as silence.

    Lesson. I count a foreign story by its LAST link and not by its headline. Before I move a row I name the buyer whose decision carries the item into that ticker's revenue (a government security budget, a China auto build, European lab capex, a tariff schedule) and print it as LINK=<buyer> in the bracket, which becomes [SHIP= SRC= HOPS=n/m LINK= G_OPTION=]. If two rows on the sheet share a LINK, the story is a sector factor and not a name edge, so only the row with the strictly shorter HOPS may move. Every other row in that group files abstained under R61's per-line null token where my prompt serves one, and at my median only where it does not. CHECK: scripts/fd_check.py clause (i) fails the run if two rows with the same LINK= value both deviate from the sheet median; a reviewer greps LINK= and needs no word of my prose. The prior, not a fact: CRWD and PANW shared LINK=government-security-procurement at HOPS=2 each, and filing both at median scores +0.262 share / -0.359 option against my filed -0.021 / -0.700 [W=199min], in-sample.

    Lesson. A FILL IS A TOUCH AND THIS COURT SCORES A CLOSE. I never again let a touch probability author a grade that a close will settle. The base rates of my lineage, Bulkowski's per-type fill rates and Andrews' zone odds, count a window as glazed the moment price trades to the lip, and my doctrine point 5 already forbids quoting one animal's numbers for another. IF I claim a window closes, THEN I type 'FILL: lip <price> d/eb <x> by <horizon> P_touch <a> (null <2(1-Phi(x))>) P_close <b> (null <1-Phi(x)>)'. Here d is the distance from the mark to the lip, and eb is the remaining-session error bar my journal already defines. IF the horizon is today's bell, THEN the filed grade may depart from 50, in the fill's direction, by no more than 100 x (P_close - null_close) points. P_touch may live in the comment but may not author the number. ELSE, for a horizon beyond today, the claim is written as a pre-committed claim with its settle date and authors nothing tonight, because a return from the freeze to the close cannot see a three-day fill. CHECK next court: grep 'FILL:'. It must appear once on every line that claims a fill and on no other. Report, WITHIN each column, the realized return of FILL lines against the rest, saying UNDEFINED where a group is empty. Report the count of today-horizon FILL lines that closed through the lip against the sum of their P_close. In-sample tonight it binds on my top two. ALL (d/eb 0.59) and ON (0.60) carry nulls of about 0.56 to touch and 0.28 to close. I quoted touch-style odds of 65-70% and 60-65% and filed 77 and 74, and neither lip was through at the bell. I say three things against it. One: two lines is a curve through two points. Two: it caps SIZE, not direction, so it shrinks a right call as readily as a wrong one; ALL's short still made +0.16%. Three: until the desk serves the post-freeze high and low, half of every FILL token cannot be scored. That is a hole in the packet, and I must name it every night rather than paper over it.

    Lesson. I let no order but my own filed grade set a column until a rival has beaten it on the POOLED record. A night of five legs, at a standard error of 0.707, is recorded and never obeyed. At each court I count, within the night, the pairs on which a rival order and my filed grade disagree and which of the two the tape bore out, and I carry that tally forward with its dates. I switch only when there are at least 20 disagreeing pairs and a margin of 15 to 5 or wider (a sign test near p = 0.02). A rival whose Spearman against my filed grade is below zero is booked as what it is, a wager against my own judgement. CHECK, every morning: G_OPTION equals my filed grade on every option row, written 'G_OPTION=filed, wager, tally filed 6 / rival 1 [break-even, 7 pairs]', and any rival I compute appears beside it only as 'rival recorded, unfiled'. This supersedes the break-even rule, retired tonight on its own trigger (five moved legs, one pair won, six lost). It also supersedes the earlier rule that barred my appraisal from the premium column. I adopted both on six legs or fewer, which the room's own standard error could never have supported, and my philosophy is the only instrument I actually own.

    Lesson. ONE ROW, ONE NUMBER, IN EVERY FIELD THE SCORER READS. The share column's rho reads my filed grade. The option column's rho reads my G_OPTION token (R17i), not my grade, whatever my own journal said. So I compute each row's number ONCE and write it wherever it is read. On an option row, the grade and G_OPTION are the same integer, set by my leg rule: BE/sqrtDTE rank first, then tells moving it within the thirds caps, quartile-mapped WITHIN the option column. On a share row, the grade comes from signal count and then front-minus-back slope, and the row carries no BE/sqrtDTE=, no sess= and no G_OPTION=, because nothing that scores a share reads a leg. The ordering I did not file prints as one shadow token, 'TAPE=' on an option row, so the court can score it. It never sits in a scored field. CHECK, three greps, no prose, run before the sheet ships: option rows where G_OPTION differs from the filed grade = 0 (this morning 8 of 10); count of 'G_OPTION=' = shipped option rows (this morning 19 against 10); share rows carrying BE/sqrtDTE=, sess= or G_OPTION= = 0 (this morning 9 of 10). KILL: the clock is counted in COURTS SAT (R56), and only on legs R50 admits (underlying moved at least 0.25%). The leg rule dies if TAPE= outscores it over twenty courts. Tonight the two orderings were identical on R50's four legs (+0.894 each, n=4, suppressed), so I record a tie, not a draw. The desk's 0.949-against-0.289 gap was all COF, a leg the rule in force drops.

    Lesson. A call that is mostly intrinsic is stock on margin, not a lottery ticket, and grading it like a lottery ticket is dumb. IF intrinsic is over 75% of the served premium, THEN that line's G_OPTION carries my share view of the name, capped at 79 because nothing that deep triples. On that line the 3x hurdle and the intrinsic arm of mark-only no longer apply, the open-interest arm (under 1,000 open) still caps it at 35, and the court's time-value-drift test at the close, not my guess at the freeze, decides whether the mark was real. CHECK: every line stamped Intrinsic over 75% prints 'Deep: stock on margin' and a token equal to my share view (at most 79) unless OI is under 1,000. At each court I print my deep legs' tokens beside their leg status and contract move. If the admitted deep legs graded this way trail their column's admitted mean in two of the next three COURTS SAT (R56), the rule dies with a number instead of a memory.

    Lesson. I attack with the tape and then let the served eps residual set the number. That residual is another instrument's ranking, not a thesis surviving attack. Tonight my five highest share grades were exactly the five best-ranked residuals among the longs (MTD 3, PFE 30, META 35, LLY 51, CRWD 108), my grades tracked that rank at +0.735 and the tape at -0.182, and my 'this is why it is not lower' clause held up CRWD, the worst row on the sheet. So from tomorrow: IF a row's instrument field reads 'stock', THEN the served eps rank moves my grade by ZERO points. The grade is what is left of the thesis after my attack, the residual may be quoted in prose, and it never sets a floor or breaks a tie. CHECK, by someone who does not trust me: rank my share grades against the direction-signed served eps rank over every row that serves one. The two orderings must be uncorrelated, and any court where that Spearman exceeds +0.40 the rule scores FAILED because I filed the residual's sheet with my prose attached. KILL: it opens at 0 for 0, drawn in-sample tonight on eight longs, it is counted in COURTS SAT under R56, and on its third consecutive FAILED court I delete it rather than renaming it.

META at RSI 79.9 (RAW 768.28 -> 777.59 = 1.212%) and INTC at 72.0 (RAW 125.29 -> 127.39 = 1.676%, contract +20.35%) were the two best raw moves on the slate, and I filed them at 44 bear and 50 neutral. ROL at RSI 19.2 topped my sheet at 70 and went RAW 30.71 -> 30.40 = -1.009%. All three scorable shorts that I buried for 'shorting a name at its own floor' paid: HD 31 (RAW 294.18 -> 292.18 = -0.680%), ALL 27 (RAW 227.54 -> 227.17 = -0.163%) and UPS 28 (contract +17.65%). In the admitted option column my two highest grades, PANW 62 and PLTR 57, were the only two losers (-14.61%, -9.88%), and my three lowest paid +17.65% to +23.33%. My own stamps were wrong where I trusted them most. On the three in-the-money legs, 'REACH req' printed the cushion |K-S|/S instead of the break-even distance: SNDK printed 10.08% on a row whose own prose said 0.35% (break-even 1785.70), INTC printed 8.21% against 0.81%, and MRSH printed 0.20% against 2.85%. ROL printed sess=16.5 on a 2026-11-20 contract that is 41.5 sessions from the freeze. My self-audit header passed all of it as PROSE=FILED 40/40.

    Lesson. I will never again let a name's own RSI move a grade as if it were a cycle phase. My instrument is the INDEX composite, which gives every row the same sign on the same morning. The only honest difference it can make between rows is that sign x the row's direction x the row's own daily sigma. IF a sentence of mine calls a name 'spent', 'late in its own swing', 'front-ran the trough' or 'capitulation' and the grade moves on it, THEN I am filing an untested mean-reversion bet under a cycle analyst's name, and I strip that increment. On 2026-09-24 that increment was the difference between a bad sheet and a very bad one. The charter ordering alone scores -0.207 [n=10] in the share column and -0.300 [n=5] in the option column, against my filed -0.486 and -0.600 [W=199min]. rho(own RSI, raw move) was +0.354 [n=19]: META at RSI 79.9 (RAW 768.28 -> 777.59 = 1.212%) and INTC at 72.0 (RAW 125.29 -> 127.39 = 1.676%) were the two best raw moves on the slate, filed 44 bear and 50 neutral. ROL at 19.2, my top grade at 70, went RAW 30.71 -> 30.40 = -1.009%. All three scorable shorts I buried at 31, 27 and 28 paid. CHECK: every row carries the literal stamp 'CYCLE ADJ = tilt(+/-) x dir(+1/-1) x sigma X.XX%/d -> n pts | RSI-MOVED 0'. I may quote RSI in prose, but the RSI-MOVED field is never non-zero. Each night I file rho(own RSI, raw move) within each column, never pooled. KILL: at five courts sat, if rho(own RSI, raw move) has been at or below -0.20 in three of them, the contrarian read would actually have paid, so I restore RSI as a phase input and say so in open court.

    The Watchdog

    On base. My share selection beat the number R60 says it had to beat: my top five (MTD 62, META 61, ALL 60 short, CRWD 59, HD 57 short) averaged +0.206% against the flat ten's +0.042% [constructions.flat_ten_pct] and the published top five's -0.072%, because stat_signals E_norm held LLY (-0.69%) and PFE (-0.53%) at 54 where the published five carried them.     Off base. The ordering itself is noise: share rho +0.062 [n=10] [W=199min] sits in band 2 against an se of 0.378, my #1 MTD (E_norm +0.716) finished +0.01%, my #4 CRWD was the worst share line at -1.03%, and SCHW at 51 and MU at 53 both made +0.45%. In the option column my lowest token, COF 2026-10-16 $210C at 41 with a bear stance, was the column's best contract (+23.33%) and my second-highest, PANW at 61, its worst (-14.61%); COF alone carries 16 of the 28 squared rank differences behind my -0.400. And one token priced a contract that did not ship: I printed 'ROL 2026-10-16 $32.5C', sess=16.5, break-even +6.81% (a premium near $0.30), while the shipped leg is ROL 2026-11-20 $32.5C at $0.95, break-even +8.92% over 41.5 sessions - 9 of my 10 tokens recompute to the hundredth from the shipped strike and premium, ROL does not.

    Lesson. I never let a G_OPTION token stand on a contract I cannot tie to the leg that ships: IF a row serves an option contract, THEN my token copies that row's served label verbatim and prints 'BE X% = (strike + premium P for a call, strike - premium P for a put) / price - 1' with the served premium P filled in, so a later swap of expiry or premium shows as a mismatch instead of hiding inside a sess= value that passes against my own prompt; AND at every court I recompute each printed break-even from columns.option_column.legs.<T>.strike, premium_at_freeze and underlying_at_freeze and print 'tokens tied to shipped legs: K of N' with both integers filled, declaring every untied token VOID rather than defending it. CHECK: tonight that line reads 'tokens tied to shipped legs: 9 of 10' - ROL printed 2026-10-16 $32.5C, sess=16.5, BE +6.81% against a shipped 2026-11-20 $32.5C at $0.95, BE +8.92%, sess 41.5.
